comment: The one-implementation registry: every shared component the product has agreed to build once,
and the single directory it lives in. An entry here is a promise that no second file exports a
symbol of that name, and the check enforces both halves — the home exists, and nothing else
claims the name. Add a component here the moment its contract is agreed, not once it is built:
the whole value is that the name is taken before somebody else takes it.
`pending` marks a home that is being written right now. Its absence is a notice rather than a
failure, and the mark must come off the moment the home lands — an entry excused forever is an
modalShellsComment: The homes allowed to compose a modal panel out of the Dialog / AlertDialog / Sheet parts.
Everywhere else, a modal surface is one of the shells — RecordWindow for reading and changing a
record, ActionDialog for an act asked of a reader — and the `hand-composed-modal` rule says so.
This list is deliberately NOT 'every registered component'. Being registered means a component
is built once; it does not mean anything inside it is exempt. A registered component can hold a
confirmation that should be an ActionDialog, and RecordAttachments does — which is why it
carries an allowance below rather than an entry here.
Adding a home here is the reviewed act of declaring a NEW modal surface. Do not add one to make
a screen pass; a screen is not a shell.

modalShells.reason: the shell an act is asked for in.
the shell a record is read and changed in.

the print preview, which layers ABOVE a record window rather than replacing it and undoes the panel's centring and cap for the printed page. A third surface, deliberately: it is not an act asked of a reader and shoehorning it into ActionDialog would put print rules inside the shell every other panel shares.
the shared unsaved-work question both shells ask, which is an AlertDialog by construction.

allowancesComment: Pre-existing debt, declared out loud. Every entry here is a REAL violation that predates the
rule catching it: the status register and the placeholder ruling both landed after the code
below was written, and the files belong to slices that are open right now. An allowance is not
a way to make a rule quiet — it is a way to let the rule bite on new work while the debt stays
on screen, printed on every run.
Two things keep the list honest, and they are checked: every entry carries a reason, and an
entry whose violation is gone is itself a failure. So fixing one of these means deleting its
line here in the same commit, and the list can never fill up with entries nobody re-reads.
An entry matches on rule + file + text (line numbers move; the violation does not). For a
placeholder the `text` is the ghost text itself, so changing the wording re-arms the rule.
The alternative escape, for a NEW placeholder that is genuinely right, is the repository's
inline `fitness-allow: <justification>` comment on the line above — a reviewed edit in the
file itself, which is where an argument about one field's wording belongs.

allowances.reason: A calendar grid is a table of DAYS, not of records: its columns are weekdays, its cells are days holding entries, and its recipe (calendar-grid.css) sizes rows by the week rather than by a row of facts. The <table> is there for its semantics, a screen reader announcing the weekday column over each day, and none of DataTable's machinery (sorting, filters, selection, totals) applies; the mc-table recipe's cell padding, hover tint and row rule would fight the day cell. It is the design system's own presentation, registered above as CalendarGrid, and the one place a raw table stands.

Belongs to the OTHER shell. It reads a record — the fee arrangement in force, its terms, and its version history — and its one act (Amend) opens a different panel. That is RecordWindow's shape: a record pane, a history tab, and an action bar. Migrating it to ActionDialog would be the wrong shell, and a read-only ActionDialog kind would be a second answer to 'read a thing'.

not an act asked of a reader — a launcher, and the documented Command-in-a-Dialog pattern this package prescribes. It stays as it is; the allowance records that the decision was made rather than missed.
a Sheet, and an edge panel holding a change history is context rather than an act. It stays; the allowance records that a Sheet was considered and left alone.

predates the rule; a sort written locally over the presentational primitives, with the remainder, offsite and totals rows held outside it by hand. It should be a DataTable.Grid — the Grid's row groups and scope-honest totals row already model the three rows this table keeps outside its sort — and that port is a design round on the firm-usage surface, reviewed on the deployed site, not a lint fix.
